images.title: Only height tells
images.purpose: Show that in a bar graph only the height of a bar carries the value, so bars have equal widths and width means nothing.
images.composition: Two bars of identical width side by side on a plain baseline, a grey width bracket under both and a purple height marker beside the taller one, lots of white space.
images.exact_structure: Two vertical bars on one baseline with the same width and a clear gap. Left bar teal #0072B2 exactly 4 units tall, right bar amber #E69F00 exactly 2 units tall. A grey #6B7280 bracket below the baseline spans both bar widths, showing equal width. A reddish purple #CC79A7 vertical arrow beside the left bar spans its full height. Exactly 2 bars, 1 bracket, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars of different widths, or any triangle or tapered shape
images.takeaway: Height shows the value; width tells us nothing about it.
images.description: Two equal-width bars with heights 4 and 2 units, a grey bracket marking the equal widths and a purple arrow marking the height.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which feature of the bars they compare, and why the widths are kept the same.

image_decisions.why: Keeping width equal makes height the only feature that carries meaning.
